title: NYC Home Improvement Contractor License Exam
page_numbering: PDF page index (1 = first page of the PDF file); null for HTML pages

questions.question: How many questions are on the DCWP Home Improvement exam?
questions.explanation: The exam has 30 multiple-choice questions.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: The exam consists of 30 questions. You must answer a minimum of 21 questions correctly to pass.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of correct answers needed to pass the Home Improvement exam?
questions.explanation: You must answer no fewer than 21 of the 30 questions correctly (70%).

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: To pass the exam, you must correctly answer no fewer than 21 questions.

questions.question: For a corporation applying for an HIC license, how many people must pass the Home Improvement exam?
options: Every employee who will sell jobs
Only one, such as an officer or 10%+ shareholder
questions.explanation: Only one qualifying person (sole proprietor, general partner, officer, principal, director, member, or 10%+ shareholder) needs to pass.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: Only ONE of the following persons needs to pass the Home Improvement Exam

questions.question: A shareholder can be the person who takes the HIC exam if he or she owns at least what share of company stock?
questions.explanation: A shareholder owning 10% or more of the company's stock may be the exam taker.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: corporate officer, principal, director, member, or shareholder owning 10% or more of company stock

questions.question: What does the HIC license application fee include with respect to the exam?
options: Nothing; the exam is always billed separately
The cost of taking the exam up to two times
questions.explanation: The application fee covers up to two exam attempts.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: The license application fee includes the cost of taking the exam up to two times.

questions.question: An HIC applicant fails the exam twice. What must they do to try again?
options: Pay the full license fee again
questions.explanation: After two failures you must pay $50 to retake the exam.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: If you fail the exam twice, you must pay $50 to retake the exam.

questions.question: How many additional exam attempts does the $50 HIC retake fee cover?
questions.explanation: The $50 fee includes two additional attempts.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: The $50 fee includes two additional exam attempts.

questions.question: Once your information appears in ExamBuilder's system, how long do you have to take and pass the exam?
questions.explanation: You have 60 days from the time your information appears in ExamBuilder's system.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: You have 60 days to take and pass the exam from the time your information appears in ExamBuilder’s system.

questions.question: How soon can you schedule the exam after DCWP processes your completed HIC application?
questions.explanation: It takes 24 hours for your information to reach ExamBuilder, so you can schedule 24 hours after processing.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: You can schedule the exam 24 hours after DCWP has processed your completed license application

questions.question: Which company administers all DCWP licensing exams?
questions.explanation: ExamBuilder administers all DCWP licensing exams.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: ExamBuilder administers all DCWP licensing exams.

questions.question: After failing a first attempt, how long must you wait before scheduling a second attempt?
questions.explanation: You must wait 24 hours from the failed attempt before scheduling again.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: You must wait 24 hours from your failed attempt before scheduling the exam for a second attempt.

questions.question: What is the deadline to reschedule a DCWP exam?
options: Noon on the day of the exam
5:00 p.m. the day before the exam
One week before the exam date
questions.explanation: Requests for a new date must be made by 5:00 p.m. the day before.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: you must request a new exam date by 5:00 p.m. the day before the originally scheduled exam date.

questions.question: What happens if you miss a scheduled exam without rescheduling in advance?
options: Nothing, if you call within a week
questions.explanation: A no-show counts as a fail, and ExamBuilder reports it to DCWP.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: If you miss a scheduled exam without rescheduling in advance, you will automatically fail

questions.question: If you miss your exam because of an emergency, how soon must you contact DCWP to request an excused absence?
questions.explanation: Contact DCWP within two business days after the missed exam day.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: within two (2) business days following the day of the exam that you missed to request an excused absence

questions.question: What identification must you bring to the ExamBuilder Test Center?
options: One government-issued photo ID with your signature
questions.explanation: Bring one government-issued photo ID that shows your signature.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: You must bring one (1) form of government-issued photo identification with your signature.

questions.question: Must a contractor who is renewing an HIC license retake the Home Improvement exam?
options: No, the exam is for new applicants only
Only if the business changed its name
questions.explanation: The Home Improvement exam is required of new applicants only.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: Home Improvement Contractor (NEW applicants only)

questions.question: Where do applicants who were granted a language accommodation take the exam?
options: The DCWP Licensing Center at 42 Broadway
questions.explanation: Applicants with a granted language or disability accommodation test at the DCWP Licensing Center, 42 Broadway.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: Applicants granted a language-related accommodation will take the exam at the DCWP Licensing Center: 42 Broadway, New York, NY 10004.

questions.question: What are ExamBuilder Test Center hours?
options: 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., seven days a week
10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday to Saturday
questions.explanation: Test centers in multiple locations citywide are open 9 to 5, seven days a week.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: Test Centers are open from 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. seven days a week in multiple locations citywide.

questions.question: When do you learn your Home Improvement exam result?
options: Right after you finish the exam
After DCWP reviews it within 10 days
questions.explanation: ExamBuilder gives you your score and pass/fail result when you finish.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: ExamBuilder will provide you with the exam results, including your score and result, i.e., Pass or Fail, after you finish your exam.

questions.question: In how many languages besides English is the Home Improvement Examination Guide available?
questions.explanation: The guide is offered in English and 11 additional languages.

source.title: DCWP Frequently Asked Questions: Exams (PDF)
source.quote: The Guide is in English and 11 additional languages.

questions.question: Which of these is one of the four areas the Home Improvement exam covers?
questions.explanation: The four areas are the basics of the law, contracts and cancellations, advertising and selling practices, and general industry and business knowledge.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: III. Advertising and Selling Practices

questions.question: How long is an HIC license term, and when does it expire?
questions.explanation: HIC licenses run 2 years and expire on February 28 of odd-numbered years.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: License Period: 2 years Expiration Date: February 28 in Odd Years

questions.question: What is the license fee for a full 24-month HIC license (applying March 1 to August 31 of an odd year)?
questions.explanation: Applying in that window costs $200 for a license valid for up to 24 months.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: Pay $200 for a license expiring February 28 of the next odd year.

questions.question: What does it cost to join the Home Improvement Business Trust Fund?
questions.explanation: The Trust Fund enrollment fee is $200.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: The fee for joining the Trust Fund is $200.

questions.question: If a contractor does not enroll in the Trust Fund, what must it submit instead?
options: A copy of a $20,000 surety bond
questions.explanation: Contractors that do not join the Trust Fund must submit a $20,000 surety bond naming DCWP as certificate holder.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: If you do not enroll your business in the Trust Fund , you must submit a copy of a $20,000 Surety Bond

questions.question: When do Trust Fund participants who stay in the Fund NOT have to pay again at license renewal?
options: When the licensee has had no consumer complaints in two years
When the Fund paid out less than $200,000 in the prior year
When the Fund held more than $2 million as of July of the prior year
When the licensee has stayed in the Fund for ten straight years
questions.explanation: Remaining participants skip the payment if the Fund had more than $2 million as of July of the prior year.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: do not have to pay again when renewing their license if the Fund had more than $2 million as of July

questions.question: Are payments into the Home Improvement Business Trust Fund refundable?
options: No, they are nonrefundable as long as the Fund exists
Yes, on request at any time
questions.explanation: Payments are held in trust and are nonrefundable as long as the Fund exists.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Business Trust Fund Enrollment (PDF)
source.quote: are nonrefundable as long as the Fund exists.

questions.question: If the Home Improvement Business Trust Fund dissolves, what happens to the money?
options: It is split equally among contributors licensed at that time
It returns to the original contributors with interest
It is paid to consumers with open complaints
It goes to the City's general fund
questions.explanation: Fund monies are distributed equally to contributors who are licensed when the Fund dissolves.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Business Trust Fund Enrollment (PDF)
source.quote: If the Fund dissolves, Fund monies will be distributed equally to Fund contributors who are licensed at the time the Fund dissolves.

questions.question: Which rule section governs the Home Improvement Business Trust Fund?
questions.explanation: The Trust Fund rules are in 6 RCNY § 2-224.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Business Trust Fund Enrollment (PDF)
source.quote: Additional information is available under 6 RCNY § 2-224.

questions.question: Who must be named as certificate holder on the workers' compensation insurance certificate submitted with an HIC application?
options: The consumer whose home is being worked on
The Department of Consumer and Worker Protection
questions.explanation: The insurance certificate must name DCWP, at 42 Broadway, as certificate holder.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: The Insurance Certificate must name the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection as the certificate holder

questions.question: Are ACORD forms acceptable as proof of New York State workers' compensation coverage for an HIC license?
questions.explanation: DCWP does not accept ACORD forms as proof of workers' compensation coverage.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: ACORD Forms are not acceptable proof of New York State workers’ compensation coverage.

questions.question: In the EPA certification requirement for HIC applicants, what does RRP stand for?
questions.explanation: RRP is the EPA Renovation, Repair, and Painting certification.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: EPA Renovation, Repair, and Painting (RRP) certification

questions.question: A contractor affirmed it needs no EPA lead certification, then takes on work that requires one. How soon must it notify DCWP?
options: Within 30 days, by sending a copy of the EPA course receipt
At the next license renewal, on the renewal application
Within five business days, with proof of certification
Only if DCWP asks, by producing the certificate on request
questions.explanation: The HIC Affirmation commits the business to notify DCWP within five business days and include proof of certification.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Contractor Affirmation (PDF)
source.quote: I will notify DCWP of the change within five business days and include proof of certification.

questions.question: With which company do HIC principals schedule fingerprinting?
questions.explanation: Fingerprinting appointments are made through IdentoGO.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: must schedule an appointment with IdentoGO to be fingerprinted

questions.question: Which tax-related number must an HIC applicant provide?
options: A Department of Buildings contractor registration number
A New York State commercial rent tax account number
A federal employer identification number from the IRS
A sales tax identification number (or its application confirmation number)
questions.explanation: Applicants submit a Sales Tax Identification Number or an Application Confirmation Number.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: Sales Tax Identification Number OR Application Confirmation Number

questions.question: A utility bill submitted as proof of business address must be dated within what period?
questions.explanation: Utility bills must be dated within the last 90 days.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: Utility bill, dated within the last 90 days

questions.question: Which state office must an LLC or corporation applying for an HIC license be registered and active with?
options: The New York State Division of Corporations
questions.explanation: Corporations, LPs, LLCs and LLPs must register and stay active with the NYS Division of Corporations.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: must register and remain active with the New York State Division of Corporations

questions.question: A sole proprietor operates under a name other than their own. What certificate do they need?
options: A Certificate of Authority from DOB
questions.explanation: Sole proprietors using another name must have a Business/Assumed Name Certificate.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: Sole proprietors operating under a name other than your own must have a Business/Assumed Name Certificate.

questions.question: What fee is added when HIC license fees are paid by credit card?
options: No fee is added for card payments
questions.explanation: Card payments carry a nonrefundable 2% convenience fee.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: You will be charged a nonrefundable 2% Convenience Fee.

questions.question: What is required before work to raise, lift, elevate or move a house?
questions.explanation: Raising, lifting, elevating or moving a building requires a special inspection by the Department of Buildings.

source.title: DCWP: Home Improvement Contractor License Application Checklist
source.quote: Work to raise, lift, elevate, or move a house or building requires a special inspection by DOB.

questions.question: What must a contractor obtain to haul waste from its home improvement jobs?
options: A Department of Sanitation commercial pickup contract
A DCWP general trucking license for each vehicle used
A Class One Self Hauler Registration from the Business Integrity Commission
A Department of Transportation dumpster and container permit
questions.explanation: Hauling your own waste requires a Class One Self Hauler Registration from BIC.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: you must obtain a Class One Self Hauler Registration from the New York City Business Integrity Commission

questions.question: Which agency issues permits for sidewalk work?
questions.explanation: Sidewalk work requires a DOT permit.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Sidewalk work requires a permit from DOT.

questions.question: Which agency should a contractor contact for a permit to place a dumpster on the street?
questions.explanation: Street dumpster permits come from DOT.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: A contractor should contact the Department of Transportation (DOT) for a dumpster permit.

questions.question: Under the Examination Guide's definition, which of these is home improvement work?
options: Installing a new fence at a house
questions.explanation: Home improvement includes work on basements, driveways, fences, garages, landscaping, patios, porches, sidewalks, pools and terraces of residential property.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: including basements, driveways, fences, garages, landscaping, patios, porches, sidewalks, swimming pools, and terraces

questions.question: Is installing central air conditioning in a home considered home improvement?
options: No, it is HVAC trade work
questions.explanation: Home improvement includes installation of central heating or air conditioning.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: installation of: • Central heating/air conditioning

questions.question: Which of these is NOT home improvement under the Guide?
options: Building a new garage at a house
questions.explanation: Construction of a new home or building is excluded from the definition.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Construction of a new home or building

questions.question: Painting an apartment, with no other home improvement services, is:
questions.explanation: Painting or decoration alone, with no other home improvement services, is not home improvement.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Painting or decoration of a building, residence, home, or apartment when no other home improvement services are provided

questions.question: Work on a residence owned or controlled by the state or a municipality is:
options: Not home improvement under the law
Home improvement only if federally funded
questions.explanation: Work on a residence owned or controlled by the state or a municipality is excluded.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Work performed on a residence owned or controlled by the state or municipality

questions.question: A store sells windows but neither arranges nor takes part in installing them. Is that home improvement?
options: Only if the windows are custom-made
questions.explanation: Selling goods or materials without arranging or participating in installation is not home improvement.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The sale of goods or materials where the seller neither arranges nor participates in the installation

questions.question: Can a subcontractor be a "contractor" under the home improvement law?
options: Only if it signs the consumer contract
Yes, whether prime contractor or subcontractor
Only if it is a corporation
questions.explanation: A contractor is anyone doing or soliciting home improvement, whether prime contractor or subcontractor.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: whether or not the contractor is a prime contractor or subcontractor

questions.question: Under the definition, must a home improvement contract be written to count as a contract?
options: No, it is an agreement whether or not in writing
questions.explanation: The definition covers agreements whether or not in writing (though the rules then require a written contract).

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: is an agreement, whether or not in writing, between a contractor and an owner or tenant

questions.question: Since August 9, 2020, how does DCWP treat Home Improvement Salespersons?
questions.explanation: Local Law 31 of 2020 repealed the salesperson license.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: As of August 9, 2020, DCWP no longer licenses Home Improvement Salespersons.

questions.question: Below what job value is a person exempt from needing a DCWP HIC license?
questions.explanation: A person performing a home improvement job of less than $200 does not need a license.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: A person performing a home improvement job, which is less than $200

questions.question: Which of these does NOT need a DCWP HIC license?
options: A licensed plumber doing plumbing work
A company selling and installing siding
questions.explanation: Plumbers and electricians acting within the scope of their licensed craft are exempt.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Plumbers and electricians acting within the scope of their licensed craft

questions.question: Does a salesperson employed by a licensed contractor need a separate DCWP license?
questions.explanation: An individual employee of the contractor, including a salesperson, does not need a license.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: An individual employee who works for the contractor, including a salesperson

questions.question: Where must a contractor display its HIC license?
options: At the entrance of every job site, facing the street
Only on its website, next to the license number
In its office where all consumers can see it, or shown on request
On the windshield of every truck the business operates
questions.explanation: Post the license in your office where consumers can see it, or show it on request.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: You must post your license in your office where all consumers can see it or show it to consumers upon request.

questions.question: What must a contractor do before a change of ownership (management)?
options: Notify DCWP in advance and get approval
File with the Department of Buildings
questions.explanation: A change of ownership needs advance notice to, and approval from, DCWP.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: You must notify DCWP in advance to get approval for a change of ownership (management).

questions.question: A contractor operates from two places of business. How many HIC licenses does it need?
options: Two, one for each place of business
None for the second if it is a warehouse
questions.explanation: A separate HIC license is required for each place of business.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: A separate Home Improvement Contractor license is required for each place of business.

questions.question: How long must a contractor keep contracts and business records?
options: 10 years, regardless of any guarantee or warranty
3 years from the date of the contract, in all cases
1 year after the job is completed and paid in full
6 years, or the length of any contractual guarantee if longer
questions.explanation: Keep records for six years or the length of any contractual guarantee, whichever is longer.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: for six (6) years or the length of time of any contractual guarantee, whichever is longer.

questions.question: What may a contractor use a consumer's payments for while the job is underway?
options: Any expense of the business, as long as it is recorded
Only expenses directly related to that home improvement
Paying down the business's earlier debts and loans
Payroll and materials for the contractor's other jobs
questions.explanation: Funds received must be used to pay expenses directly related to that home improvement.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The home improvement contractor must use all funds received to pay expenses directly related to the home improvement.

questions.question: When may a contractor use a consumer's funds for unrelated expenses?
options: After the job is completed and all labor, material and subcontractor costs are paid
Once the consumer signs the certificate of completion
As soon as the three-day cancellation period has passed
Once at least half of the contracted work has been done
questions.explanation: Only when the job is completed and all direct expenses for it have been paid.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: unless the home improvement is completed and all expenses for direct labor, material, and subcontractors related to the home improvement have been paid.

questions.question: When may a contractor start the contracted work?
options: As soon as the consumer's deposit check has cleared
After the three-day cancellation period expires without cancellation
Right after both parties sign the contract and the copy is given
As soon as the consumer signs the permit disclosure
questions.explanation: No work or changes to the property until the three-day cancellation period has expired without cancellation.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Home Improvement Contractors (PDF)
source.quote: until after the three-day cancellation period has expired and the consumer has not exercised the right of cancellation.

questions.question: Under what name may a licensed contractor do business?
options: Any name registered with the state
Only the business name or DBA listed on the license
Any name, if the license number is shown
questions.explanation: Doing business under any other name than the one on the license is prohibited.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Conduct the home improvement business in any name other than the name of the business or Doing Business As (DBA) name listed on the license.

questions.question: May a home improvement contractor arrange a home improvement loan for a consumer?
options: Yes, if it is disclosed in the contract
No, contractors cannot arrange such loans
Yes, but only through a licensed bank
questions.explanation: Contractors may not act as agent for, advertise, promote or arrange home or home improvement loans.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Act as an agent for, or advertise, promote, or arrange a home loan or a home improvement loan for the consumer.

questions.question: Which of these is prohibited conduct for a contractor?
questions.explanation: Contractors cannot abandon or fail to perform agreed-upon work.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Abandon or fail to perform agreed-upon work.

questions.question: Must a contractor give a consumer a written estimate?
options: Only if the consumer pays in advance
Yes, if the consumer requests one
questions.explanation: A written estimate must be provided when the consumer asks for one.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Yes, if the consumer requests one.

questions.question: A contractor charges a fee for an estimate. What must it do?
options: Refund it if the consumer does not sign the final contract
Bill it separately after the job is done, outside the price
Keep it under $50 and collect it in cash before the visit
Disclose the fee before the estimate and itemize it in the total estimated price
questions.explanation: The fee must be disclosed beforehand and included and itemized in the total estimated contract price.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: disclose the fee to the consumer before you provide the estimate and you must include and itemize the fee in the total estimated contract price

questions.question: What civil fine can apply for each day of unlicensed home improvement activity?
questions.explanation: Civil fines of up to $100 per day apply to unlicensed activity or aiding it.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: faces fines of up to $100 per day for engaging in unlicensed activity or aiding and abetting

questions.question: Besides fines, what can DCWP do about unlicensed home improvement work?
options: Padlock the business and confiscate tools and trucks
questions.explanation: DCWP can padlock and confiscate tools and trucks used for unlicensed work.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: DCWP can padlock (close down) and confiscate (take) the tools and trucks used in connection with unlicensed home improvement work.

questions.question: What can happen to a contract entered into after a contractor's misrepresentations?
options: It becomes binding only on the consumer
It is automatically extended by 30 days
It may be voided, with restitution ordered
Nothing, as long as the work is completed
questions.explanation: Such a contract may be voided and the contractor ordered to pay restitution.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: a contract entered into after misrepresentations are made may be declared null and void, and a contractor may be ordered to pay restitution

questions.question: Operating a home improvement business without a license may be what kind of offense?
questions.explanation: Operating without a license, or while suspended or revoked, may be a misdemeanor.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: may be guilty of a misdemeanor and may be prosecuted criminally

questions.question: What form must every home improvement contract take?
options: Written, signed by the contractor only
In writing and signed by everyone involved
questions.explanation: Every contract must be in writing and signed by everyone involved.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Every home improvement contract must be in writing and signed by everyone involved.

questions.question: When must the consumer receive a copy of the contract?
options: At signing and before any work is done
questions.explanation: Give a completed, legible copy at signing and before any work.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: You must give the consumer a completed, legible copy of the contract at the time of signing and before any work is done.

questions.question: A contractor makes its sales pitch in Spanish. In what language(s) must the contract be?
questions.explanation: If another language was used in the oral sales presentation, the contract must be in that language and in English.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: unless another language was used in any oral (spoken) sales presentation, in which case the contract needs to be in that language and in English.

questions.question: A consumer wants work beyond the original contract. What should the contractor provide?
options: A note in the contractor's records
A written change order signed by both parties
questions.explanation: Additional work requires a written amendment, a change order, signed by both.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The contractor should provide a written amendment to the contract, known as a change order, which the consumer and the contractor must both sign.

questions.question: What must a change order include, per DCWP's inspection checklist?
options: The consumer's initials and a new three-day cancellation notice
The DOB permit number and the name of each subcontractor
The cost of the extra work, the new contract price and when payment is due
Only a short description of the extra work, without prices
questions.explanation: Change orders must show the added cost, the new contract price and the payment due date.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Home Improvement Contractors (PDF)
source.quote: The change order must include the cost of the additional work, the new contract price, and the date when payment is due.

questions.question: Under DCWP's model contract, when must the consumer get a copy of a signed change order?
options: Only if the consumer asks for one in writing
Within 30 days after the change order is signed
Before the additional or changed work starts
Together with the final invoice when the job is done
questions.explanation: The contractor gives the consumer the signed change order before starting the changed work.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Estimate, Contract and Forms (PDF)
source.quote: The Contractor shall provide the Consumer with a copy of the signed Change Order form before starting the additional or changed work.

questions.question: Under DCWP's model change order form, when are extra charges for a change order due, unless agreed otherwise in writing?
options: Before the contractor begins the change in work
questions.explanation: Unless otherwise agreed in writing, extra charges are due before the change in work begins.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Estimate, Contract and Forms (PDF)
source.quote: extra charges for a Change Order shall be due before the Contractor begins the Change in Work

questions.question: Which contractor detail must appear in a home improvement contract?
questions.explanation: The contract must show the contractor's name, office address, telephone number and DCWP license number.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: the contractor’s name, office address, telephone number, and DCWP license number.

questions.question: Which dates must the contract give?
options: Only the date the contract was signed
Approximate start and substantial completion dates
Only the dates when each payment is due
The expiration dates of all required permits
questions.explanation: Contracts state approximate dates when work will begin and be substantially completed.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Approximate dates when work will begin and be substantially completed

questions.question: If the parties agree that a definite completion date is "of the essence," what must the contractor do?
questions.explanation: An agreed essential completion date must be noted in the contract.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Home Improvement Contractors (PDF)
source.quote: If you and the consumer have agreed that a definite completion date is of the essence, you must note this in the contract.

questions.question: How must the contract describe the materials the contractor will provide?
options: Including make and model number and other identifying information
By general category, such as "standard windows"
By supplier name only, without models or brands
It need not describe materials if the price is stated
questions.explanation: Materials, including appliances, must be described with make, model number and other identifying information.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Home Improvement Contractors (PDF)
source.quote: include materials’ make and model number and any other identifying information.

questions.question: What lien notice must the contract give the owner?
options: The contractor waives any lien rights once the deposit is paid
An unpaid contractor or subcontractor may have a claim enforceable against the property
Only the consumer's mortgage lender can file a lien on the home
Liens can be filed only on commercial, not residential, work
questions.explanation: The contract warns that unpaid contractors or subcontractors may have a claim enforceable against the property under lien laws.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Home Improvement Contractors (PDF)
source.quote: the contractor or subcontractor who performs work and is not paid may have a claim against the consumer which may be enforced against the property

questions.question: Under the Lien Law notice in the contract, what is the contractor required to do with payments received before completion?
options: Spend them on any costs of running the contracting business
Forward them to DCWP to hold until the job is completed
Deposit them (or post a bond or contract of indemnity instead)
Hold them in cash on site until the job is finished
questions.explanation: The contractor must deposit pre-completion payments, or instead post a bond or contract of indemnity with the consumer.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Home Improvement Contractors (PDF)
source.quote: the contractor is legally required to deposit all payments received prior to completion of work

questions.question: Which New York State law section is cited in the contract notice about depositing payments?
questions.explanation: The notice cites subdivision 4 of Section 71-a of the NYS Lien Law.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Home Improvement Contractors (PDF)
source.quote: in accordance with subdivision 4 Section 71-a of New York State’s Lien Law

questions.question: If a contract has progress payments, how must each advance payment relate to the work?
options: It must bear a reasonable relationship to the work performed
It must be paid in cash
It must equal one third of the price
It may be any amount the contractor sets
questions.explanation: Each advance payment must bear a reasonable relationship to the work performed.

source.title: DCWP HIC Contractual Compliance Agreement and Checklist (PDF)
source.quote: each advance payment must bear a “reasonable relationship” to the work performed

questions.question: What must the contract say about workers' compensation?
options: Workers' compensation coverage is optional for small home jobs
The consumer must carry insurance covering the contractor's workers
The contractor will show proof of coverage at final payment
The contractor will furnish a Certificate of Workers' Compensation Insurance before beginning work
questions.explanation: The contract must state that the contractor will furnish the certificate before work begins.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The contract must inform the consumer that the contractor will furnish a Certificate of Workers’ Compensation Insurance before beginning work.

questions.question: A contractor is exempt from carrying workers' compensation insurance. What must it give the consumer?
options: Nothing, since exempt contractors have no paperwork to share
A signed letter from its accountant explaining the exemption
A copy of the Certificate of Attestation of Exemption from the NYS Workers' Compensation Board
A copy of its DCWP license, which shows the exemption status
questions.explanation: Exempt contractors give the consumer the WCB Certificate of Attestation of Exemption.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Home Improvement Contractors (PDF)
source.quote: you must give the consumer a copy of the Certificate of Attestation of Exemption from the New York State Workers’ Compensation Board.

questions.question: Where in the contract must the "YOU, THE BUYER, MAY CANCEL" statement appear?
questions.explanation: The cancellation statement goes directly above (in immediate proximity to) the signature lines.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The contract must include the following statement directly above the signature lines

questions.question: What is the minimum type size for the contract's cancellation statement?
questions.explanation: The statement must be boldface and at least 10 point.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: This statement must be in boldface, and the font size must be at least 10 point.

questions.question: Until when may a buyer cancel a home improvement contract?
options: Midnight of the third business day after the transaction
Midnight of the third calendar day
questions.explanation: The buyer may cancel any time before midnight of the third business day after the transaction date.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: YOU, THE BUYER, MAY CANCEL THIS TRANSACTION AT ANY TIME PRIOR TO MIDNIGHT OF THE THIRD BUSINESS DAY AFTER THE DATE OF THIS TRANSACTION.

questions.question: How many copies of the Notice of Cancellation form must be attached to the signed contract?
questions.explanation: Two copies (in duplicate) of the completed Notice of Cancellation must be attached.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: the contractor must attach to the signed contract two copies of a separate, completed form titled “Notice of Cancellation.”

questions.question: How must the Notice of Cancellation be attached to the contract?
options: On the back of the signature page
So that it is easily detachable
questions.explanation: The notice is attached to the contract and easily detachable.

source.title: DCWP HIC Contractual Compliance Agreement and Checklist (PDF)
source.quote: which will be attached to the contract and easily detachable.

questions.question: After a valid cancellation, within how many business days must payments be refunded?
questions.explanation: Honor a valid cancellation and refund all payments within 10 business days.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: The contractor should honor any valid notice of cancellation and must within 10 business days:

questions.question: After cancellation, the buyer makes delivered goods available, but the seller does not pick them up. When may the buyer keep or dispose of them?
options: After 20 days from the cancellation notice
questions.explanation: If the seller does not pick up within 20 days of the notice, the buyer may keep or dispose of the goods.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: DOES NOT PICK THEM UP WITHIN 20 DAYS OF THE DATE OF YOUR NOTICE OF CANCELLATION, YOU MAY RETAIN OR DISPOSE OF THE GOODS

questions.question: If a cancelling buyer follows the seller's shipping instructions to return goods, who bears the cost and risk?
questions.explanation: Return shipment under the seller's instructions is at the seller's expense and risk.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: REGARDING THE RETURN SHIPMENT OF THE GOODS AT THE SELLER’S EXPENSE AND RISK.

questions.question: Besides the written notice, how else must the contractor tell the consumer about the right to cancel?
options: By text message after work starts
Orally, at the time of signing
By certified mail a week later
questions.explanation: The contractor must also tell the consumer orally at signing.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: A contractor must tell the consumer at the time of contract signing about the right to cancel

questions.question: If the contractor never gives the required oral and written cancellation notices, how long may the consumer cancel?
questions.explanation: Until the contractor complies, the consumer may cancel the contract.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Until the contractor complies with the requirements for oral and written notice of the consumer’s right to cancel, the consumer may cancel the contract.

questions.question: After a cancellation, what must the contractor tell the consumer about materials already delivered?
options: Whether it intends to repossess or abandon them
That the consumer must pay for them
questions.explanation: Within 10 business days the contractor must say whether it will repossess or abandon delivered materials.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Notify the consumer as to whether the contractor intends to repossess or abandon any shipped/delivered materials.

questions.question: May a contract say the consumer waives rights or remedies under the law?
questions.explanation: Contracts cannot state that the consumer waives or cannot assert legal rights, claims, defenses or remedies.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Home Improvement Contractors (PDF)
source.quote: The contract cannot state that the consumer is waiving, giving up, or is prohibited from asserting any rights, claims, defenses, or remedies

questions.question: May a contractor ask the consumer to sign a certificate of completion before the work is done?
options: Yes, to speed up final payment
Yes, if the job is 90% complete
Yes, with a written promise to finish
questions.explanation: Asking for a completion certificate before the work is actually completed is prohibited.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Home Improvement Contractors (PDF)
source.quote: You cannot ask the consumer to sign a certificate of completion before you actually completed the work.

questions.question: May a contractor perform work not described in the contract?
options: Only with the consumer's written consent
questions.explanation: Work that is not in, or differs from, the contract needs the consumer's written consent.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Home Improvement Contractors (PDF)
source.quote: You cannot perform work that is not in the contract, or is different from the work described in the contract, without the consumer’s written consent.

questions.question: How does DCWP count violations when a contract is missing several required items?
options: Only the first missing item counts
Each missing item is a separate violation
questions.explanation: Each missing contract requirement is a separate violation with its own penalty.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Home Improvement Contractors (PDF)
source.quote: Each missing contract requirement is a separate violation for which a penalty will be assessed.

questions.question: What right may homeowners insist on if the contractor fails to start work on time?
options: To cancel for a full refund after an agreed number of days past the start date
To withhold half the contract price until the work is done
To charge the contractor a daily fee until work begins
To have DCWP assign another contractor to finish the job
questions.explanation: Homeowners can insist the contract let them cancel for a full refund if work is not started within an agreed number of days after the start date.

source.title: DCWP HIC Contractual Compliance Agreement and Checklist (PDF)
source.quote: Homeowners have the right to insist that the contract entitle them to cancel for a full refund if the Contractor fails to start the work

questions.question: Under DCWP's model contract, who is responsible if the contractor fails to pay subcontractors or suppliers it arranged?
questions.explanation: The contractor pays the subcontractors and vendors it arranged; the consumer is not responsible if it fails to.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Estimate, Contract and Forms (PDF)
source.quote: The Consumer is not responsible if the Contractor fails to pay these subcontractors or supply vendors.

questions.question: What is the legal claim an unpaid contractor or supplier may have against the property called?
questions.explanation: An unpaid contractor, subcontractor or supplier may have a mechanic's lien against the property.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Estimate, Contract and Forms (PDF)
source.quote: who is not paid may have a valid legal claim against your property known as a mechanic’s lien.

questions.question: How can a consumer file a complaint about a contractor, per the model contract?
options: Only by certified letter to DOB
Call 311 or go online to nyc.gov/dcwp
questions.explanation: Complaints can be filed by calling 311 or online at nyc.gov/dcwp.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Estimate, Contract and Forms (PDF)
source.quote: The Consumer may file a complaint regarding the Contractor’s performance or the job by calling 311

questions.question: Which 2025 local law added the home improvement permit disclosure requirement?
questions.explanation: DCWP's 2026 rule implements Local Law 181 of 2025, which added the permit disclosure.

source.title: DCWP: New Laws and Rules
source.quote: implement Local Law 181 of 2025, which adds a new disclosure requirement for home improvement contractors relating to permits.

questions.question: What must the written permit notice tell the owner about checking on permits?
options: How to appeal a permit denial to DCWP
The DOB plan examiner's direct phone number
Nothing; verification is the owner's job
How to verify permit status in City databases
questions.explanation: The notice must explain how the owner can verify permit status through City databases such as DOB's system.

source.title: DCWP HIC Contractual Compliance Agreement and Checklist (PDF)
source.quote: Instructions on how the owner can verify the status of such permits through New York City databases

questions.question: For which kinds of work may a DOB permit be needed, per DCWP's inspection checklist?
options: Plumbing, electrical work, pointing and home extensions
Only painting, wallpapering and other decorative work
Only window cleaning and other routine maintenance
Only landscaping, fencing and other outdoor yard work
questions.explanation: DOB permits may be needed for plumbing, electrical work, pointing, extensions and other work.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Home Improvement Contractors (PDF)
source.quote: You may need to obtain a permit from the New York City Department of Buildings (DOB) for plumbing, electrical work, pointing, home extensions

questions.question: Which agency issues permits for an addition or alteration to a house?
questions.explanation: Permits for additions and alterations come from DOB.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: A contractor secures all necessary permits from the New York City Department of Buildings (DOB).

questions.question: Who must file alterations to building plans with DOB?
options: A DCWP inspector after a site inspection
A registered architect or licensed engineer
The homeowner, signing as the owner of record
questions.explanation: A registered architect or licensed engineer must file plan alterations with DOB.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: a registered architect or licensed engineer must file alterations to building plans with DOB.

questions.question: Before starting a home extension, what should a contractor do first?
options: Collect the full contract price up front
Ask DOB staff for a zoning opinion on the plan
Consult a licensed architect or engineer about zoning
Order the materials to lock in current prices
questions.explanation: First consult a licensed architect or engineer (not DOB) on whether the extension complies with zoning.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: consult with a licensed architect or engineer—not DOB—to determine if the owner can put in the extension

questions.question: Who files an amended Certificate of Occupancy at DOB?
options: A registered architect or professional engineer
The contractor's salesperson or office manager
A DCWP inspector after a final inspection
questions.explanation: The actual amended Certificate of Occupancy must be filed by a registered architect or professional engineer.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: A registered architect or professional engineer must file the actual amended Certificate of Occupancy at DOB.

questions.question: What must all HIC advertising and sales literature contain?
options: The owner's home address and personal phone number
A statement of the lifetime warranty offered
The DOB permit number for each job advertised
The DCWP Home Improvement Contractor license number
questions.explanation: All advertising and sales literature must show the DCWP license number.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: All advertising and sales literature must contain the DCWP Home Improvement Contractor license number.

questions.question: If a licensee emails consumers, what must the email contain?
questions.explanation: Licensees that use email with consumers must include the license number in the email.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials (PDF): License Enforcement laws and rules for all DCWP licensees
source.quote: If a licensee uses email to communicate with consumers, the licensee's email must contain the license number

questions.question: An ad lists a price, but installation costs extra. What must the ad do?
options: Nothing, if the price is accurate
Show installation in small print only
questions.explanation: If installation is extra, the ad must clearly say so.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: If installation is extra, the ad must clearly say so.

questions.question: When may a contractor advertise "Factory to you" or "Buy from manufacturer"?
options: If it buys directly from a factory
Only if it actually makes or produces the items
questions.explanation: Those claims are allowed only when the contractor actually makes or produces the items.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: You cannot make statements such as “Factory to you” and “Buy from manufacturer” unless you actually make or produce the items.

questions.question: May a contractor offer a "lifetime" guarantee?
options: Yes, if the guarantee is backed by a surety bond
Yes, but only for roofing and siding work
No; guarantees may extend only to the item's normal life
Yes, as long as the guarantee is given in writing
questions.explanation: Lifetime guarantees are prohibited; guarantees may cover only the normal life of the item or service.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: You cannot make “lifetime” guarantees or warranties.

questions.question: For defective materials and workmanship, how long may a guarantee run?
options: At least ten years for all materials and labor
Exactly one year from the date of completion
Any length the contractor chooses to offer
No longer than the period within which the defect is likely to show up
questions.explanation: A defect guarantee cannot extend beyond the period within which the defect is likely to appear.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: you cannot make the guarantee beyond the period within which the defect is likely to show up.

questions.question: What is the rule for a "savings" claim in an ad?
options: It is banned entirely in home improvement ads
It must state the savings as a percentage only
It must be approved in advance by DCWP
It cannot imply the amount specified is the selling price
questions.explanation: A savings claim cannot suggest that the stated savings amount is the selling price.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: A “savings” claim cannot imply the amount specified is the selling price.

questions.question: A contractor advertises that its windows cut energy bills by 40%, without proof. This is:
options: Allowed, if the ad adds an asterisk and fine print
Allowed, since it is ordinary sales puffery
Allowed, if the window maker made the same claim
Prohibited, since benefit claims must rest on known and provable facts
questions.explanation: Ads cannot claim benefits that are not based on known and provable facts.

source.title: DCWP Inspection Checklist: Home Improvement Contractors (PDF)
source.quote: Advertisements cannot make claims that your products or services will result in benefits that are not based on known and provable facts.

questions.question: What is the rule for ad headings?
options: They must be in capital letters
They must not contain exaggeration or deception
questions.explanation: Headings must not exaggerate or deceive.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Headings must not contain exaggeration or deception.

questions.question: May an unlicensed person advertise home improvement services in NYC print or broadcast media?
options: Yes, if the license is pending
questions.explanation: People required to be licensed who are not licensed may not advertise those services.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials (PDF): License Enforcement laws and rules for all DCWP licensees
source.quote: who is not so licensed may not advertise the availability of goods and services related to the carrying on of such trade

questions.question: What distinguishes an employee from a subcontractor?
options: An employee always holds its own DCWP license
An employee works for wages under direct supervision
A subcontractor works for wages under supervision
There is no legal difference between the two
questions.explanation: An employee works for wages under direct supervision; a subcontractor is in business for itself.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: An employee works for wages and is under the employer’s (prime or subcontractor) direct supervision and control.

questions.question: Must a subcontractor doing home improvement work in NYC have a DCWP license?
options: No, the prime contractor's license covers it
Only if it signs with the consumer
questions.explanation: A subcontractor, unlike an employee, must have its own DCWP license.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: A subcontractor, as opposed to an employee of a general contractor, must have a DCWP license to perform home improvement work in New York City.

questions.question: Which agency licenses electricians and plumbers in NYC?
questions.explanation: DOB licenses electricians and plumbers.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: DOB licenses electricians and plumbers.

questions.question: What is the net profit of a job?
questions.explanation: Net profit is the final profit of any job after expenses.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Net profit is the final profit of any job after expenses.

questions.question: Which insurance must cover a contractor's employees?
options: None for crews of fewer than 5 workers
questions.explanation: Employees must be covered by workers' compensation and disability insurance.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: You must cover employees with Workers’ Compensation and disability insurance.

questions.question: What are a contractor's tax duties for employees?
options: Report wages to the IRS and withhold taxes
Pay a flat City payroll fee
questions.explanation: Employers report employee wages to the IRS and withhold taxes.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: You must report employee wages to the Internal Revenue Service (IRS), and you must withhold taxes.

questions.question: What do federal immigration laws require of employers?
options: Registering every employee with DCWP each year
Nothing for contractors with few employees
Ensuring employees have legal authority to work in the US
questions.explanation: Employers must ensure employees are legally authorized to work in the United States.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: comply with the federal immigration laws, which require employers to ensure that employees have legal authority to work in the United States.

questions.question: When must a home improvement contractor use a licensed electrician?
options: Only in commercial buildings, not in private homes
To install anything having to do with light, heat and power, regardless of voltage
Only for work above 120 volts, such as dryers and ranges
Only when adding new circuits to the electrical panel
questions.explanation: A licensed electrician must install anything to do with light, heat and power, at any voltage.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: You must use a licensed electrician to install anything having to do with light, heat, and power, regardless of voltage.

questions.question: How must a contractor handle sales tax on repairs?
options: Collect it only on materials over $500
questions.explanation: Contractors must collect sales tax on repairs from the consumer.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Contractors must collect sales tax for repairs from the consumer.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of a capital improvement?
options: Adding a bathroom to a home
questions.explanation: Adding a bathroom is a capital improvement; repairs and painting are not.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Adding a bathroom to a home is an example of a capital improvement.

questions.question: Is repairing a window frame a capital improvement?
options: Only if the frame is replaced in wood
questions.explanation: Repairs such as fixing a window frame or painting do not qualify as capital improvements.

source.title: DCWP Home Improvement Examination Guide (PDF)
source.quote: Repairs such as repairing a window frame or painting the living room do not qualify as capital improvements.

questions.question: How soon must a licensee respond in writing to a complaint DCWP sends it?
options: Only if a hearing is scheduled
questions.explanation: Respond in writing within 20 days of the date DCWP sends the complaint.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials (PDF): License Enforcement laws and rules for all DCWP licensees
source.quote: The response must be made within 20 days of the date the complaint is sent to the licensee or applicant

questions.question: A renewal application filed how late is treated as a new license application?
options: Sixty days or more after expiration
questions.explanation: Renewals filed 60 or more days after expiration are treated as new applications.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials (PDF): License Enforcement laws and rules for all DCWP licensees
source.quote: filed sixty days or more after the expiration date of such license shall be treated as a new license application

questions.question: How soon must a licensee satisfy a consumer's judgment related to licensed activity (absent a stay, appeal or agreed schedule)?
options: Within 30 days of entry of the judgment
questions.explanation: Judgments must be satisfied within 30 days of entry unless stayed, appealed, or on an agreed schedule.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials (PDF): License Enforcement laws and rules for all DCWP licensees
source.quote: within thirty (30) days from the date of entry of the judgment

questions.question: How soon must a licensee reply to a DCWP subpoena or document request?
options: Only after a court orders it
questions.explanation: Replies are due within twenty days of the date the request was mailed or served.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials (PDF): License Enforcement laws and rules for all DCWP licensees
source.quote: A licensee must reply to a subpoena, a request for documents or interrogatories within twenty days

questions.question: If required business records are lost or stolen, when must the licensee report it to DCWP?
options: Within ten calendar days, by affidavit
questions.explanation: Loss or theft of required records must be reported by affidavit within ten calendar days.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials (PDF): License Enforcement laws and rules for all DCWP licensees
source.quote: within ten calendar days of such loss or theft.

questions.question: Can a DCWP license be sold or transferred to another business?
options: No, unless law or rule specifically allows it
questions.explanation: Licenses are not assignable or transferable unless specifically provided by law, regulation or rule.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials (PDF): License Enforcement laws and rules for all DCWP licensees
source.quote: No license issued under chapter two shall be assignable or transferable unless otherwise specifically provided

questions.question: If DCWP charges unlicensed activity starting on a given date, what does the law presume?
options: It happened only on that one date, unless more is proven
The activity continued every day through the hearing, unless rebutted
Nothing; DCWP must prove each day separately
It stopped on the day the notice was served
questions.explanation: There is a rebuttable presumption that unlicensed activity continued daily without interruption.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials (PDF): License Enforcement laws and rules for all DCWP licensees
source.quote: there shall be a rebuttable presumption that the unlicensed activity continued every day, without interruption

questions.question: Where must a licensee appear to answer a DCWP notice of hearing?
options: Housing Court in the borough of the business
Small Claims Court in the consumer's borough
The Department of Buildings hearing office
The Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings (OATH)
questions.explanation: Licensees answer notices of hearing at OATH.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials (PDF): License Enforcement laws and rules for all DCWP licensees
source.quote: A licensee must appear at the Office of Administrative Trials and Hearings to answer a notice of hearing

questions.question: After a licensee fails to renew, how soon must it destroy its DCWP license and ID documents?
questions.explanation: Former licensees must destroy license and identification documents within 10 business days of expiration.

source.title: DCWP Educational Materials (PDF): License Enforcement laws and rules for all DCWP licensees
source.quote: not later than 10 business days after the expiration of such license, destroy all license and identification documents
